messages:
sophia: Heads up — we've got a spike in fncall schema rejections. Dashboards show a big bump in `strict_reject` and the traffic is getting routed to the degen path, but billing/quotas are attributing it to customers incorrectly :confused:
kevin: Can you paste an example payload or log snippet? wondering if the validator is losing the route_id during the handshake
sophia: Sure — example request + validator log:
```
Request: {
  \"model\": \"gpt-4o\",
  \"fn_call\": {
    \"name\": \"create_ticket\",
    \"arguments\": {
      \"title\": \"Login fail\",
      \"priority\": \"high\"
    }
  }
}
Validator log: [2026-03-12T15:07:21Z] validator.py: WARN missing route_id, falling back to degen-route (reason: strict_schema_fail)
```
jamal: that log line is the smoking gun. if route_id is missing we tag it as degen and the quota billing pipeline picks the fallback route (which is wrong). we should prefer a validation-specific telemetry tag instead of degen
elaine: from console UX POV we also need to show that a request was rejected for schema vs actually hitting quota. right now Operators see a single graph and assume quota violation :eyes:
kevin: proposal: when validator fails, emit metric `invoke.reject_reason=validation_strict` and include `orig_route_id` (if available) and `validation_schema` in the event. then update routing step to not mark degen-route for billing attribution. small change but should fix dashboards and chargeback mismap
sophia: I like that. would it be expensive to add `orig_route_id` to the validator? jamal?
jamal: cheap. validator already gets the handshake metadata. I can add a non-blocking tag in the validation event. two caveats: 1) some connectors strip metadata, 2) we need to backfill current spike buckets for analysis
elaine: UX asks: can we surface both fields in the console event details (reject_reason + route_id) and add a tooltip explaining "validation rejects do not consume customer quota"? Product will ❤️ that.
kevin: rollout plan: add metric + tag in validator (non-breaking), flip dashboard to use `invoke.reject_reason` for graphing, then change billing pipeline mapping to prefer `orig_route_id` when reject_reason==validation_strict. start in canary on eng-us-east only
sophia: sounds good. let's also add a quick alert on count(delta 5m) > 50 for validation_strict so we notice regressions
jamal: I'll open a tiny PR for the validator emit + tests. tag me for code review @kevin and @sophia.
console-team: re: dashboard changes — we'll add a separate panel for validation rejects and a tooltip. need the metric name exactly so we can query it. what prefix do you want? `invoke.reject_reason` as a tag or `invoke.reject_reason:validation_strict` as a metric?
kevin: use `invoke.reject_reason` tag on the common `invoke.event` metric. query example for datadog: `count by reject_reason (invoke.event{env:prod, reject_reason:*})`
console-team: copied. ETA to update dashboard 1 day after PR merges.
sophia: can we also emit a short structured example in the logs to help SRE triage: `validator_meta: {reject:validation_strict, orig_route: <id or null>, sample_request_id: <id>}`
jamal: yeah will include that. will also add a small sampling flag to avoid logspam — sample 10% by default, 100% if reject spikes > 100/min
sophia: perfect. thanks. I'll monitor the canary and update #incidents if anything looks off :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: canary deploy queued — validator:emit-tags v1.2 -> eng-us-east at 2026-03-12T18:30:00Z (CI green)
kevin: ack. after canary we should validate dashboards and billing mappings with a synthetic run (I'll script 200 invalid fncalls and check attribution)
sophia: great plan. assigning follow-ups: jamal -> validator emit PR, console-team -> dashboard panel + tooltip, kevin -> synthetic test script. will reconvene if the canary spikes.
elaine: thanks all :pray:
